item.title: U.S. launches new airstrikes in southern Iran amid stalled ceasefire talks
item.description:
The U.S. military carried out new airstrikes in southern Iran targeting a military site believed to pose a threat to American forces and commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, a U.S. official confirmed on Wednesday. U.S. forces also intercepted and shot down multiple Iranian drones in the region, according to ABC News.

The strikes come as negotiations between Washington and Tehran over a potential peace deal remain unsettled. Speaking at a cabinet meeting Wednesday, President Donald Trump said Iran "wants very much to make a deal" but added, "We're not satisfied with it, but that we will be. Either that or we'll have to just finish the job".

item.title: Iran's IRGC says it struck US airbase near Bandar Abbas
item.description:
The United States and Iran exchanged fresh military strikes on Thursday near the Strait of Hormuz, the most serious escalation since a ceasefire took effect on April 8, rattling energy markets and casting doubt over negotiations to end the conflict.

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it targeted a US airbase early Thursday from which American forces had launched strikes on southern Iran near Bandar Abbas airport, according to Reuters and the Tasnim news agency. The IRGC described the attack as "a serious warning" to the United States. US Central Command had previously carried out what it termed "self-defense strikes" targeting missile launch sites and Iranian vessels attempting to lay mines near the strait.

item.title: Israel strikes Beirut suburb targeting Iranian militia missile commander
item.description:
Israel's air force carried out a targeted strike on the Choueifat area on the outskirts of Beirut's southern suburbs on Thursday afternoon, the first such attack near the Lebanese capital in weeks, as the military said it was targeting the head of the missile unit in the Imam Hussein Division, an Iran-linked militia operating alongside Hezbollah.

The target was identified as Ali al-Husseini, described by Israeli Army Radio as the commander of the rocket system within the Imam Hussein Division. It was not immediately clear whether al-Husseini was killed in the strike. The attack hit a building in Choueifat, with at least one person reported killed and several wounded, according to Lebanese media reports.

item.title: US and Iran reportedly reach 60-day MOU deal awaiting Trump's approval
item.description:
Negotiators from the United States and Iran have reached an agreement on a 60-day memorandum of understanding to extend their ceasefire and begin negotiations over Iran's nuclear program, but President Donald Trump still needs to give final approval, Axios reported on Thursday, citing two U.S. officials.

The reported breakthrough came on a day of renewed violence. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it struck a U.S. airbase early Thursday in retaliation for American strikes near the port city of Bandar Abbas, where U.S. forces had intercepted four Iranian attack drones and hit a ground-control station threatening commercial shipping near the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Anthropic raises $65B at $965B valuation, topping OpenAI
item.description:
Anthropic has closed a $65 billion Series H funding round at a post-money valuation of $965 billion, making it the most valuable AI startup in the world and surpassing rival OpenAI, Bloomberg reported on Thursday.

The round was co-led by Altimeter Capital, Dragoneer, Greenoaks, and Sequoia Capital, with additional participation from Capital Group, Coatue, and D1 Capital Partners. The deal caps a whirlwind fundraising process that began in late April, when Anthropic first signaled to investors it was targeting a valuation above $900 billion.

item.title: US to designate Brazil's two largest gangs as terrorist organizations
item.description:
The United States announced Thursday that it will classify Brazil's two largest criminal organizations — the Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC) and the Comando Vermelho (Red Command) — as Foreign Terrorist Organizations, a move that carries sweeping financial and legal consequences and is expected to deepen friction between Washington and Brasília.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in a statement that the formal FTO designation will take effect on June 5. In the meantime, the State Department has already classified both gangs as "Specially Designated Global Terrorists," immediately subjecting them to U.S. sanctions.

item.title: Japan calls Russian criticism of its military buildup 'ridiculous' at UN
item.description: Japan's UN ambassador on Thursday rejected Russia's criticism of Japan's defense expansion as "ridiculous," pushing back against Moscow's accusations during a UN Security Council open debate on upholding the principles of the UN Charter.

item.title: Vance says US and Iran 'very close' to ceasefire deal
item.description:
Vice President JD Vance told reporters on Thursday that the United States and Iran are "very close" to finalizing a memorandum of understanding that would extend their ceasefire for 60 days, reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and restart nuclear discussions — but cautioned the two sides are "not there yet."

The remarks came as Axios reported that US and Iranian negotiators have reached consensus on the terms of the MOU, though the agreement remains unsigned pending approval from President Trump and Iran's supreme leadership. Trump has been briefed on the proposal but has requested "a couple of days" to deliberate before giving his final endorsement.

item.title: US denies Iran's claim it destroyed American aircraft in Bushehr
item.description: Iran's state television reported early Friday that a US aircraft was destroyed in the Jam governorate of Bushehr province in southern Iran, citing local governor Masoud Tangestani. A US official denied the claim to Reuters, stating no American aircraft had been shot down near Bushehr, and no independent confirmation of the Iranian report has emerged.

item.title: Hungary's Magyar vows 'reliable' NATO role but won't arm Ukraine
item.description: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte met with Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar in Brussels on Thursday to discuss preparations for the alliance's upcoming summit in Ankara, as Budapest seeks to rebuild its standing within the transatlantic alliance while maintaining its refusal to arm Ukraine.

item.title: Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket explodes during test at Cape Canaveral
item.description:
A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded during an engine-firing test at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station on Thursday evening, sending a fireball into the night sky and rattling homes across the surrounding area. No injuries were reported.

The explosion occurred around 9 p.m. at Launch Complex 36, where residents of Cape Canaveral and Cocoa Beach felt tremors and soon flooded social media with images of the blast. Blue Origin confirmed the incident in a brief statement: "We encountered an anomaly during today's hotfire test. We will share updates as we gather more information."

Jeff Bezos responded on X, writing: "It's too early to determine the underlying cause, but we are already investigating. Today has been challenging, but we will reconstruct whatever needs to be rebuilt and resume our flights. It's worth the effort."

item.title: Suspected Russian drone strikes building in Romania, injuring two
item.description:
A suspected Russian attack drone struck a residential apartment building in the Romanian border city of Galati early on May 29, causing an explosion and injuring at least two people, according to Romanian media reports and social media accounts from the scene.

The incident occurred during an overnight Russian drone assault targeting Ukraine's Odesa region, which shares a border with Romania's Galati county. Romanian news outlet MediaFax reported that the drone impacted the building, with two people sustaining injuries. Fighter jets were scrambled in response, and Romanian authorities dispatched forensic teams and explosives experts to investigate.

item.title: US-Iran draft deal includes $300B reconstruction fund for Tehran
item.description: A draft memorandum of understanding between the United States and Iran contains a proposed $300 billion reconstruction and investment program for Tehran, according to an Iranian lawmaker and reporting from The New York Times, adding a striking economic dimension to the emerging framework aimed at ending the three-month-old war.

item.title: China building 80-plus launch pads near nuclear silos
item.description:
China is constructing a sprawling network of launch pads, bunkers, and communications nodes near its nuclear missile silos in the remote deserts of its northwest, according to a Reuters analysis of satellite imagery published on Friday.

The images reveal more than 80 pads that could be used by China's expanding fleet of mobile missile launchers and air-defense batteries, along with facilities that may support electronic warfare, satellite communication, and command operations, according to three security experts who reviewed the imagery for Reuters.

item.title: Trump announces lifting of naval blockade on Iran
item.description: President Trump declared on Friday that the U.S. naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz "will now be lifted," posting the announcement on Truth Social after convening in the White House Situation Room to make what officials described as a "final determination" on the deal with Iran. The announcement follows weeks of fraught negotiations and marks the most concrete step toward ending the nearly three-month conflict between the United States and Iran.

item.title: Chevron CEO says ships attacked in Strait of Hormuz this week
item.description: Chevron CEO Mike Wirth disclosed in an interview with Bloomberg TV that multiple vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz were attacked this week, including incidents not yet publicly reported, even as ceasefire optimism between the United States and Iran drove oil prices sharply lower.

item.title: Trump's Situation Room meeting on Iran ends without deal
item.description:
President Donald Trump convened a high-stakes meeting in the White House Situation Room on Friday to make what he called a "final determination" on a proposed memorandum of understanding with Iran, but the nearly two-hour session ended without a resolution, according to The New York Times.

The meeting came after Trump announced his plans in a Truth Social post Friday morning, writing, "I will be meeting now, in the Situation Room, to make a final determination". He outlined preconditions for any agreement, insisting that Iran "must agree that they will never have a Nuclear Weapon or Bomb" and that the Strait of Hormuz must "immediately open" to unrestricted shipping with no tolls.

item.title: Rubio thanks Pakistan for Iran mediation efforts
item.description: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio met with Pakistani Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar at the State Department on Friday, with discussions centering on Pakistan's role mediating the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict and the broader bilateral relationship between Washington and Islamabad.

item.title: Ebola funding pledges nearly halved as outbreak spreads
item.description:
International financial commitments to combat the Ebola outbreak in Central and East Africa have nearly halved in a matter of days, Africa CDC Director-General Jean Kaseya revealed Thursday, as the deadly Bundibugyo strain continues to spread through the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda with no approved vaccine available.

Speaking from Kinshasa, Kaseya said pledges that stood at nearly $500 million on Monday, May 25, had dropped to approximately $290 million by Thursday after multiple donors withdrew their commitments. The collapse in funding represents a loss of roughly $210 million at a moment when the outbreak has grown to more than 1,000 suspected cases and 246 deaths in the DRC alone.

item.title: Quarter of trapped oil tankers slip out of Hormuz
item.description: A slow, stealthy trickle of oil tankers has begun slipping out of the Persian Gulf through the Strait of Hormuz, with roughly one-quarter of the large non-Iranian vessels stranded since the war began now having crossed the chokepoint, even as Chevron CEO Mike Wirth warned that ships continue to come under attack.
